questions.question: Why can chunking alone make a fact impossible to retrieve correctly?
options: If a fact is cut across two chunks, no retriever can return it whole in one chunk
Chunks are always too small for embeddings
questions.explanation: Every later step works on chunks; a split fact can only be found in halves.

questions.question: Fixed + overlap kept every fact intact but found the whole fact for only 4 of 7 questions. Why?
options: The extra overlapping half-chunks compete with the good chunks in ranking
questions.explanation: Overlap mainly improves 'facts intact'; it adds near-duplicate chunks that can outrank the best one.

questions.question: Which question did only 'sections + path' answer, and why?
options: The Paris question, because it is the longest
The 'most cities' hotel limit: its section text never mentions hotels or cities; only the heading path does
The password question, because of numbers
questions.explanation: Short sections often rely on their headings for meaning. The path puts that meaning into the chunk.

questions.question: What do the two measures 'facts intact' and 'top-1 has fact' each tell you?
options: Whether the chunker kept facts whole at all, and whether retrieval then finds a chunk with the whole fact
Recall and precision of the model
questions.explanation: The first measures the chunker alone; the second measures chunker and retriever together.

questions.question: You're indexing PDFs. What should happen before chunking?
options: Parse the structure (headings, tables, lists) so the chunker can cut on it
questions.explanation: Plain text extracted from a PDF has already lost the headings a structure-aware chunker needs.

questions.question: A teammate sets chunk size to 500 tokens 'because the tutorial did'. What do you suggest?
options: Try several sizes and strategies on real questions from your corpus and pick by facts intact and retrieval hits
questions.explanation: The right size depends on how long your facts and sections are. Measure.
